title: Pacific: islands over centuries
hook: Was Pacific settlement one continuous expedition?

predict.question: What separates western and eastern settlement?

frames.heading: Near Oceania
frames.text: Lapita communities live in the Bismarck islands.

frames.heading: West Polynesia
frames.text: Settlement reaches Fiji, Tonga and Samoa.

frames.heading: Aotearoa
frames.text: Polynesian settlers reach Aotearoa New Zealand.

reveal: Scrubbing the dates reveals a long pause, not one unbroken expedition. Settlement spread into West Polynesia in the second millennium BCE; eastern archipelagos were settled much later. Aotearoa was reached around 1300 CE. These were generations of skilled navigation and settlement.
limit: Dates are approximate and revised by archaeology; arrows summarize regional movement.

sources.section: Geoff Irwin: Remote Oceania, settlement sequence and New Zealand
